```{r echo=FALSE}


# Set the file path
file_path <- "Rodrigo_Clean_data.xlsx"
setwd("~/R")
getwd()

# Load necessary libraries
library(readxl)
library(dplyr)
library(mgcv)
library(caret)
library(ggplot2)



# Step 1: Set the file path and read data
file_path <- "Rodrigo_Clean_data.xlsx"
data <- read_excel(file_path, sheet = "Sheet1")

# Step 2: Remove missing values
data_cleaned <- na.omit(data)



# Step 3: Convert categorical variables to factors
data_cleaned$treatment_lines <- as.factor(data_cleaned$treatment_lines)
data_cleaned$tx_group_drug <- as.factor(data_cleaned$tx_group_drug)
data_cleaned$sponsors <- as.factor(data_cleaned$sponsors)

# Step 4: Calculate `non_compliance` as the outcome variable
if (all(c("total_withdrew_noreason", "total_withdrew_because_noncompliance", "lost_fu", "total_number_enrolled") %in% colnames(data_cleaned))) {
  data_cleaned <- data_cleaned %>%
    mutate(
      non_compliance = ifelse(
        total_number_enrolled > 0,
        (total_withdrew_noreason + total_withdrew_because_noncompliance + lost_fu ) / total_number_enrolled,
        NA
      )
    )
  cat("The new outcome variable 'non_compliance' has been calculated and added successfully.\n")
} else {
  stop("One or more columns required for calculating 'non_compliance' are missing.")
}

# Step 5: Calculate `death_rate`
if (all(c("total_withdrew_because_death", "total_number_enrolled") %in% colnames(data_cleaned))) {
  data_cleaned <- data_cleaned %>%
    mutate(
      death_rate = ifelse(
        total_number_enrolled > 0,
        total_withdrew_because_death / total_number_enrolled,
        NA
      )
    )
  cat("The new variable 'death_rate' has been calculated and added successfully.\n")
} else {
  stop("One or more columns required for calculating 'death_rate' are missing.")
}

# Remove rows with missing `non_compliance` or `death_rate`
data_cleaned <- data_cleaned %>% filter(!is.na(non_compliance), !is.na(death_rate))



# Rename `non_compliance` to `outcome` for compatibility with the model
if ("non_compliance" %in% colnames(data_cleaned)) {
  if ("outcome" %in% colnames(data_cleaned)) {
    data_cleaned <- data_cleaned %>% select(-outcome)  # Remove existing `outcome` if it exists
  }
  data_cleaned <- data_cleaned %>% rename(outcome = non_compliance)
} else {
  stop("The new outcome variable 'non_compliance' could not be found.")
}

# Ensure `outcome` and `death_rate` are numeric
data_cleaned$outcome <- as.numeric(data_cleaned$outcome)
data_cleaned$death_rate <- as.numeric(data_cleaned$death_rate)



# Step 6: Split data into training, validation, and test sets
set.seed(123)
train_index <- createDataPartition(data_cleaned$outcome, p = 0.8, list = FALSE)
train_data <- data_cleaned[train_index, ]
remaining_data <- data_cleaned[-train_index, ]

set.seed(123)
validation_index <- createDataPartition(remaining_data$outcome, p = 0.5, list = FALSE)
validation_data <- remaining_data[validation_index, ]
test_data <- remaining_data[-validation_index, ]

#Check distribution of predictors

library(ggplot2)

# Plot numeric predictors against `outcome`
numeric_vars <- c("number_withdrew_tx_because_pod", "withdrew_txrealated_control_rate", 
                  "withdrew_txrealated_tx_rate", "death_rate")

for (var in numeric_vars) {
  p <- ggplot(data_cleaned, aes(x = .data[[var]], y = outcome)) +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.6) +
    geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "blue") +  # Linear fit
    geom_smooth(method = "gam", formula = y ~ s(x, bs = "tp"), color = "red") +  # GAM fit
    labs(title = paste("Relationship between", var, "and Outcome"),
         x = var, y = "Outcome") +
    theme_minimal()
  
  print(p)  # Ensure each plot is displayed
}

# Step 7: Fit the GAM model with the new outcome variable and `death_rate`
gam_model <- gam(
  formula = outcome ~ 
    s(number_withdrew_tx_because_pod, bs = "tp", sp = 0.5) +  # Add penalty for overfitting
    treatment_lines + 
    sponsors + 
    tx_group_drug +
    withdrew_txrealated_control_rate +
    withdrew_txrealated_tx_rate +
    s(death_rate, bs = "tp", sp = 0.5),  # Add penalty for over-fitting
  data = train_data,
  family = gaussian(link = "log")
)

# Step 8: Evaluate the GAM model
# Generate predictions for training, validation, and test sets
train_data$predicted_outcome <- predict(gam_model, newdata = train_data)
validation_data$predicted_outcome <- predict(gam_model, newdata = validation_data)
test_data$predicted_outcome <- predict(gam_model, newdata = test_data)


calculate_rmse <- function(observed, predicted) {
  sqrt(mean((observed - predicted)^2))
}

# Back-transform predictions for RMSE calculation
train_rmse <- calculate_rmse(train_data$outcome, exp(train_data$predicted_outcome))
validation_rmse <- calculate_rmse(validation_data$outcome, exp(validation_data$predicted_outcome))
test_rmse <- calculate_rmse(test_data$outcome, exp(test_data$predicted_outcome))

# 1. Calculate Baseline RMSE (predicting the mean of outcome)
baseline_prediction <- mean(data_cleaned$outcome)  # Baseline: mean of outcome
baseline_rmse <- sqrt(mean((test_data$outcome - baseline_prediction)^2))

# Print Baseline RMSE
cat("Baseline RMSE:", baseline_rmse, "\n")

# 2. Compare RMSE to Outcome Variance
outcome_sd <- sd(data_cleaned$outcome)
outcome_range <- max(data_cleaned$outcome) - min(data_cleaned$outcome)

cat("Outcome Standard Deviation (SD):", outcome_sd, "\n")
cat("Outcome Range:", outcome_range, "\n")

# 3. Compute Relative RMSE (RRMSE)
train_rrmse <- train_rmse / mean(train_data$outcome)
validation_rrmse <- validation_rmse / mean(validation_data$outcome)
test_rrmse <- test_rmse / mean(test_data$outcome)

cat("Relative RMSE (Train):", train_rrmse, "\n")
cat("Relative RMSE (Validation):", validation_rrmse, "\n")
cat("Relative RMSE (Test):", test_rrmse, "\n")

# 4. Aggregate Results for Comparison
results <- data.frame(
  Metric = c("RMSE", "RRMSE"),
  Train = c(train_rmse, train_rrmse),
  Validation = c(validation_rmse, validation_rrmse),
  Test = c(test_rmse, test_rrmse),
  Baseline = c(baseline_rmse, baseline_rmse / mean(data_cleaned$outcome))
)

# Print Results
print(results)

# Step 9: Visualize Observed vs Predicted for the Test Set
ggplot(test_data, aes(x = predicted_outcome, y = outcome)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, color = "red", linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(
    title = "Observed vs Predicted Outcomes - Test Set",
    x = "Predicted Outcome",
    y = "Observed Outcome"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

summary(gam_model)

```


```{r}
# Load necessary libraries
library(readxl)     # To read Excel files
library(dplyr)      # For data manipulation
library(mgcv)       # For GAM modeling
library(caret)      # For splitting data
library(ggplot2)    # For data visualization

# Step 1: Read the data and remove missing values
file_path <- "Rodrigo_Clean_data.xlsx"  # File path
data <- read_excel(file_path, sheet = "Sheet1") %>%
  na.omit()  # Remove rows with missing values

# Step 2: Convert categorical variables to factors
data_cleaned <- data %>%
  mutate(
    treatment_lines = as.factor(treatment_lines),
    tx_group_drug = as.factor(tx_group_drug),
    sponsors = as.factor(sponsors)
  )

# Step 3: Create derived variables (`non_compliance` and `death_rate`)
if (all(c("total_withdrew_noreason", "total_withdrew_because_noncompliance", "lost_fu", "total_number_enrolled") %in% colnames(data_cleaned))) {
  data_cleaned <- data_cleaned %>%
    mutate(
      non_compliance = ifelse(
        total_number_enrolled > 0,
        (total_withdrew_noreason + total_withdrew_because_noncompliance + lost_fu) / total_number_enrolled,
        NA
      )
    )
}

if (all(c("total_withdrew_because_death", "total_number_enrolled") %in% colnames(data_cleaned))) {
  data_cleaned <- data_cleaned %>%
    mutate(
      death_rate = ifelse(
        total_number_enrolled > 0,
        total_withdrew_because_death / total_number_enrolled,
        NA
      )
    )
}

# Remove rows with missing `non_compliance` or `death_rate`
data_cleaned <- data_cleaned %>%
  filter(!is.na(non_compliance), !is.na(death_rate)) %>%
  rename(outcome = non_compliance)  # Rename `non_compliance` to `outcome`

# Step 4: Split data into training, validation, and test sets
set.seed(123)
train_index <- createDataPartition(data_cleaned$outcome, p = 0.8, list = FALSE)
train_data <- data_cleaned[train_index, ]
remaining_data <- data_cleaned[-train_index, ]

validation_index <- createDataPartition(remaining_data$outcome, p = 0.5, list = FALSE)
validation_data <- remaining_data[validation_index, ]
test_data <- remaining_data[-validation_index, ]

# Step 5: Visualize relationships between predictors and `outcome`
numeric_vars <- c("number_withdrew_tx_because_pod", "withdrew_txrealated_control_rate", 
                  "withdrew_txrealated_tx_rate", "death_rate")

for (var in numeric_vars) {
  p <- ggplot(data_cleaned, aes(x = .data[[var]], y = outcome)) +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.6) +
    geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "blue") +  # Linear fit
    geom_smooth(method = "gam", formula = y ~ s(x, bs = "tp"), color = "red") +  # GAM fit
    labs(title = paste("Relationship between", var, "and Outcome"),
         x = var, y = "Outcome") +
    theme_minimal()
  print(p)
}

# Step 6: Fit the GAM model
gam_model <- gam(
  formula = outcome ~ 
    s(number_withdrew_tx_because_pod, bs = "tp", sp = 0.5) + 
    treatment_lines + 
    sponsors + 
    tx_group_drug +
   
    withdrew_txrealated_tx_rate +
    s(death_rate, bs = "tp", sp = 0.5),  # Add penalties to prevent overfitting
  data = train_data,
  family = gaussian(link = "log")  # Log link for nonlinear relationship
)

# Step 7: Evaluate the model
# Generate predictions
train_data$predicted_outcome <- predict(gam_model, newdata = train_data)
validation_data$predicted_outcome <- predict(gam_model, newdata = validation_data)
test_data$predicted_outcome <- predict(gam_model, newdata = test_data)

# Define RMSE function
calculate_rmse <- function(observed, predicted) {
  sqrt(mean((observed - predicted)^2))
}

# Calculate RMSE (back-transform predictions for log link)
train_rmse <- calculate_rmse(train_data$outcome, exp(train_data$predicted_outcome))
validation_rmse <- calculate_rmse(validation_data$outcome, exp(validation_data$predicted_outcome))
test_rmse <- calculate_rmse(test_data$outcome, exp(test_data$predicted_outcome))

# Calculate baseline RMSE
baseline_prediction <- mean(data_cleaned$outcome)
baseline_rmse <- calculate_rmse(test_data$outcome, baseline_prediction)

# Step 8: Compare RMSE to baseline and variance
outcome_sd <- sd(data_cleaned$outcome)
outcome_range <- max(data_cleaned$outcome) - min(data_cleaned$outcome)

cat("Baseline RMSE:", baseline_rmse, "\n")
cat("Outcome Standard Deviation (SD):", outcome_sd, "\n")
cat("Outcome Range:", outcome_range, "\n")

# Relative RMSE
train_rrmse <- train_rmse / mean(train_data$outcome)
validation_rrmse <- validation_rmse / mean(validation_data$outcome)
test_rrmse <- test_rmse / mean(test_data$outcome)

results <- data.frame(
  Metric = c("RMSE", "RRMSE"),
  Train = c(train_rmse, train_rrmse),
  Validation = c(validation_rmse, validation_rrmse),
  Test = c(test_rmse, test_rrmse),
  Baseline = c(baseline_rmse, baseline_rmse / mean(data_cleaned$outcome))
)
print(results)

# Step 9: Visualize Observed vs Predicted for Test Set
ggplot(test_data, aes(x = exp(predicted_outcome), y = outcome)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, color = "red", linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(
    title = "Observed vs Predicted Outcomes - Test Set",
    x = "Predicted Outcome",
    y = "Observed Outcome"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

# Summary of GAM model
summary(gam_model)

```
